title:
Read-only COI-driven budget + scalar-closure sufficiency probe (P2, no training).

Scope
-----
* No training, no optimizer step, no model rollout and no new prediction file.
* The only event payload read is the frozen fit297 preparation (267 stable, 30 unstable);
  val/test are never addressed and the frozen preparation must certify them closed.
* Frozen prediction ``*.npz`` and frozen model exports are read.  Writes are confined to
  ``private_data/coi_budget_20261030`` (``run``) and ``results/coi_budget_20261030``
  (``publish``); no existing file is modified.

Objects (frozen mechanical body ``M``, ``D``, ``q_p = jpi_p * storage_base``)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Model mechanical equation (``force_graph_model_20261028.ForceGraphROM.field``)::

    M * omega_dot = -grad U(delta) - D * omega + q_p * p - r,   1^T grad U = 0

With ``R1 = 1^T r / 10`` and ``W1 = 1^T omega / 10`` the mechanical inversion of the
collective hidden force under the *frozen* body is

.. math::

    1^T r_est(t) = -1^T(M*omega_dot_true) - 1^T(D*omega_true) + 1^T(q_p*p_true),

where ``omega_dot_true`` is ``np.gradient(omega_true, 0.01, axis=0, edge_order=2)``.
This is a mechanical-inversion estimate under the frozen body; it is **not** the true
hidden force, and any error of the true machine parameters (D, q_p, U) is absorbed into
it.  Only the collective component ``1^T r_est`` is defined by this inversion.

COI budget (model-M-weighted mean; the project COI convention)::

    dw_COI(t) = sum_i M_i (omega_pred_i - omega_true_i) / sum_i M_i
              = (1/sum M) int_0^t [ -1^T dr - 1^T(D*dw) + 1^T(q_p*dp) ] ds,
    dr = r_pred - r_est,  dw = omega_pred - omega_true,  dp = p_pred - p_true.

Because ``r_est`` is defined by inversion of the truth, this identity is closed by
construction up to (i) the initial COI offset ``dw_COI(0)`` (the window starts one
0.01 s step after initialisation) and (ii) finite-difference/trapezoid error.  The
informative content is therefore the three-term share and the residual scale, **not**
"closure holds".

Scalar closure sufficiency
--------------------------
``Q = lambda W + B diag(lambda_ref a_bar) B^T`` with ``B^T 1 = 0`` gives ``1^T Q = lambda 1^T``
exactly, hence ``dR1/dt = kappa W1 - lambda R1`` and ``d(1^T r)/dt = kappa 1^T omega -
lambda 1^T r``.  Driven by ``W1_true`` with the model's own ``kappa``/``lambda`` and
``R1_model(0)`` this yields ``R1_closure(t)``, compared against ``R1_est(t)``.  A
per-event best ``(kappa, lambda, R1(0))`` fit on a fixed lambda grid separates "closure
form insufficient" from "initial value / W1 trajectory wrong".  The same integrator on
the model's own trajectory (``W1_model`` -> ``R1_model``) is the implementation
self-consistency check of the exact family identity.

Acceptance checks (protocol 2026-10-30, gates 4-5)
--------------------------------------------------
* budget closure residual only at finite-difference/discretisation scale (and the
  measured initial COI offset is reported separately, never hidden);
* the scalar integrator recovers a known ``(kappa, lambda, R10)`` trajectory;
* ``r_est`` sign/index alignment is unit-tested;
* a model-trajectory cross-check (inversion of the model's own ``omega``/``p``/``r``)
  reports the finite-difference floor of the whole pipeline.

title:
EXPLORATORY / POST-HOC: p-channel error decomposition (not pre-registered).

Read-only. Frozen A128 predictions + truth on train fit297 stable events; no training,
no model rollout. The frozen model's p dynamics is a fixed linear filter of omega:

    pdot_i = -jpi_p_i * omega_i - rpp_i * storage_base_i * p_i.

We split the p error into three parts at each 0.01 s output:
    p_pred - p_true = [p_pred - F(omega_pred)]     (integration/implementation)
                    + [F(omega_pred) - F(omega_true)]  (omega-induced)
                    + [F(omega_true) - p_true]         (p-model-form)
where F(omega) is the same RK4 filter integrated from the frozen p(0). All parts are
reported in the frozen normalized metric mean_i((.)/p_scale_i)^2. The parts are not
orthogonal; a sum-of-parts / total ratio is reported.

Scope: this is a diagnostic of the fixed p channel, not a mechanism proof, not a model
decision, and it was added after the pre-registered probe results were seen.

title:
E3: causal mechanical-power ODE module (Pm own equation) on F1.

Mirrors the kron-reduce M0-GMD-PM chain, rebuilt on the kiki canonical
generator_10 dev fold (ZOH causal contract).  Three explicit stages:

  m03eg : TransientEmfM0Model      -- 3rd-order M0 with nodal transient EMF
  gmd   : GraphModalDiscoveryM0Model -- low-rank graph closure, frozen backbone
  pm    : CausalPmGraphModalM0Model  -- M0-GMD + stable GraphModalPmDynamics

The Pm port dynamics live on the zero-total-power subspace::

    a   = U_p.T (Pm - Pm_equilibrium)          U_p spans 1.T p = 0
    v   = U_p.T Pi_power(omega)
    a'  = A a + B v                            A Hurwitz (spectral margin)

Deployment evolves mechanical power causally from the clearing value Pm_clear;
the exact A=B=0 ZOH policy is a candidate and the fallback.  Gate (internal):
Hurwitz + causal H100 validation improvement >= 2% over ZOH, else ZOH stays.

Every stage runs its physics audit.  H100 source-stratified trajectory error is
reported for three policies on the same M0-GMD backbone:
  ZOH    (Pm held at Pm_clear)          -- causal baseline
  PM     (Pm from the fitted ODE)       -- causal proposed
  oracle (observed Pm schedule, linear) -- non-causal upper bound

Test is never opened; outcome labels are not used in fit/selection.

title:
E3b: Pm-ODE gate re-run on long stable (highorder) traces at H=800.

E3's H100 (1 s) gate rejected the Pm equation because a ~2.5 s governor
recovery time constant is far longer than the gate window.  This sub-experiment
re-runs ONLY the Pm stage (the frozen M0-GMD backbone is loaded from E3's

events whose traces are >= 18 s.  The dense (near-critical/unstable) events are
excluded from the gate because their long-horizon rollouts diverge by
construction; the train weak system still sees all 209 events (dense included).

Gate and causal contract unchanged: Hurwitz + tau<=2.5 s, exact ZOH fallback,

title:

Loads the pruned E2 model, runs the numeric certificate suite, computes the
integration-free candidate margin for every validation event. The candidate
search is not a verified global lower bound, so formal stability is refused;

margin rule; the rule itself reads only delta0/omega0/Pm_clear (the exact
clearing state) -- no future trajectory. A trajectory-threshold classifier on

title:

On the F1 development fold only (train=209 / val=43, test is NEVER opened),
fit each baseline from the training context (derivatives + observed Pm as
teacher) and roll it out on the full val set at H100 under the causal ZOH
deployment contract -- the exact protocol used for the modular model.  The
reference rows (M0 backbone from results/e02_backbone and the pruned modular
energy model from results/e02_prune) are re-rolled on the SAME val population
with the SAME code path so the table is internally consistent.

Results are difficulty-stratified exactly like E6/E6c (truth peak |omega| in
the first post-clear second): mild / moderate / severe.  Trajectory accuracy is
only claimed in the band where the modular model itself is accurate; severe and
unstable events are where the energy model hands over to the integration-free
margin rule, which none of these baselines can offer (certificate_claim=False).

title:
Artifact validation gate (G6).

Public API
----------
inspect_json_text(text, *, source, strict_nonfinite) -> list[Finding]
    Structural inspection of one JSON text. ``Finding`` has ``.level`` in
    {"error", "warning"} and ``.message``.
verify_json_artifacts(root=None) -> dict
    Repository-wide scan of every ``*.json`` under ``results/`` and ``configs/``.
    Returns ``{"files_checked", "status", "errors", "warnings"}``.

Semantics
---------
* duplicate object keys            -> error (always)
* non-finite numbers (NaN/Infinity/-Infinity):
    ``strict_nonfinite=True``      -> error
    ``strict_nonfinite=False``     -> warning
* malformed JSON                   -> error

The repository scan runs in *legacy* mode (``strict_nonfinite=False``): only
errors fail the gate. The inherited scientific corpus legitimately contains
``Infinity`` (e.g. an infinite effective time constant recorded for a rejected
module candidate), so non-finite tokens are warnings there, not gate failures.

CLI
---
    python experiments/verify_artifacts.py --json-only
Exit code 0 iff the repository scan reports no errors, else 1.
